prompts.uart_tx.sv: Solve the engineering task specified by spec.md. Return exactly ONE JSON object per turn, no prose or additional actions. Allowed actions: {"tool":"read","file":"spec.md"}, {"tool":"read","file":"uart_tx.sv"}, {"tool":"edit","content":"complete file"}, {"tool":"test"}, {"tool":"submit"}. Read both files before edit or submit. Only uart_tx.sv can be edited. Test runs the trusted public checker against the current file. You have at most 20 total actions and 4 public tests. Rejected actions also consume an action. Submission is allowed without passing tests and ends solving. Independent terminal and held-out results are not returned. No shell, other files, reference, checker or private inputs are available. Do not combine actions.

reason: Confirmed fixed-interface false acceptance requires separate revision3 qualification and calibration; no replacement of old trials.
fixed_conditions: Same task contracts, starting RTL, model/worker, prompt, actions, budgets and projected feedback as verifier2 cohort; only interface-validation revision and independent provider sampling differ.
stopping_rules: Stop affected cohort on source drift, isolation failure or indeterminate trusted verification. Retain all started attempts, no replacement.
Stop each trial on submit,20actions,worker error or1200seconds.
primary_questions: Can the current fixed-interface checker complete real isolated UART repair rollouts?
Does a successful submission satisfy actual decoded frames, bit durations, busy offers and adjacent frame obligations?

offline_analysis.training_selection: No use of held-out results to select candidates

estimated_resources.basis: Previous UART trial costs and actual revision2 control runs; finite bound, no adaptive expansion

interpretation: Two new exploratory trials, not replacement samples, not a tool-effect success-rate comparison. Reliability improvement rests on the controlled same-source defect recheck.
